dimension_justifications.soundness: The central replay-model certificate, terminal convention, selection protocol, and scope are presented precisely enough to assess. I did not independently re-prove the results.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is unusually explicit about what metrics do and do not mean, and Table 1/Figure 1 are readable. However, the nine-page main text devotes substantial space to dense robustness and continuous-alpha material before protocol and primary evidence, obscuring the core argument.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper offers a clearly identifiable conditional replay certificate and careful empirical comparison. Its practical scope is deliberately narrower than its title-level setting: it is not an ordered-online deployment result.

paper_summary: The paper studies early stopping for binary majority-vote rollouts under a count-exchangeable replay model. It fits a mixture over task-level pass counts, stops when posterior disagreement with the corresponding full-N binary vote is at most alpha, and evaluates replay flip/count-reduction with FIT/CAL/TEST. It characterizes synthetic ordered-drift failures and excludes chronological deployment, gold correctness, and operational savings.
strongest_verified_contribution: A coherent and scoped replay-model result: BAYES-H uses an exact per-prefix posterior flip certificate, with terminal state explicitly zero replay disagreement, and reports 80.9% replay count reduction at realized replay flip 0.0249 for alpha=0.05 on the OMR TEST readout.
strengths: Title, abstract, model definition, limitations, and conclusion consistently identify corresponding full-N binary pass-count replay vote rather than answer correctness.
The replay-versus-ordered-online boundary is repeated at points likely to invite overinterpretation.
Table 1 is compact and legible and exposes the alpha=0.10 exception where FIXED-EB has slightly higher reduction.
Figure 1 is readable; caption labels values as artifact-derived replay quantities and AI-use disclosure identifies generative composition and independent label checks.
The endpoint convention c_H(x_N,N)=0 is stated in method, theorem, and limitations.
questions: Can main text be reorganized around replay estimand/non-claim, certificate/endpoint, selection protocol, and main table before extended TV/continuous-alpha analysis?
Can authors provide one compact visual or boxed definition distinguishing replay full-vote disagreement, stopped-answer correctness, and operational compute/cancellation cost?
Which portions of critical-radius and fit-size analysis are essential to the central claim versus appendix/supplement material?

issues.location: Main text Section 4 pages 4--5 before Sections 5--6; Section 9
issues.observed_evidence: Before protocol and main table, the manuscript spends roughly two dense pages on TV-ball optimization, cross-carrier correlations, non-monotone critical-radius behavior, and continuous-alpha family counting. Limitations adds constructive repairs and coarse-fit findings. These details interrupt the simpler chain from replay estimand to certificate to selected TEST readout.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader can reconstruct the result, but density obscures the decision-relevant claim and scope within nine pages, despite a substantial appendix for robustness detail.
issues.required_fix: Reorder/compress main text so model/estimand, theorem with terminal convention, FIT/CAL/TEST protocol, Table 1, and ordered-online non-claim form the primary flow. Move continuous-alpha enumeration, detailed TV decomposition, and fit-size repair mechanics to appendix, retaining one concise robustness takeaway.
issues.verification_test: A technically literate reader can state replay estimand, stopping rule, calibration/selection split, headline result, and non-deployment boundary from first six pages without unpacking critical-radius analysis.

issues.observed_evidence: Appendix D combines a multi-series figure, thresholds, correlations, fit-size counterfactuals, and repair details in very long paragraphs. Result/interpretation/diagnostic hierarchy is difficult to recover.
issues.why_it_matters: Readers inspecting robustness boundaries face unnecessary load and may mistake descriptive diagnostics for the main guarantee.
issues.required_fix: Add an appendix roadmap and short takeaway labels; move secondary diagnostics to a compact table/supplement and visually separate guarantee, diagnostic, and repair result.
issues.verification_test: Each appendix subsection opening identifies precise guarantee/diagnostic, scope, and whether it affects the main replay claim.

ethics_concerns: No distinct ethics issue. The paper responsibly states replay metrics are not correctness, token/latency, cancellation, or ordered-online deployment measurements.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. The manuscript includes an AI-use statement for Figure 1.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A streamlined main-text narrative foregrounding estimand, endpoint, protocol, evidence, and non-deployment boundary before ancillary robustness analysis.
An appendix restructure making guarantee/diagnostic distinctions and critical-radius analysis navigable.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Any revision weakening the explicit replay versus ordered-online correctness/cost distinction.
Any title, abstract, figure, or conclusion presenting replay savings as deployed token, latency, cancellation, or answer-quality savings without new evidence.
review_limitations: This assessment is limited to the frozen snapshot and emphasizes clarity rather than independently validating all proofs or artifacts.
